Okay! Imagine you have a special kind of toy top that spins in space, where there’s no air and nothing to stop it. Now, if you make this top spin really fast along one direction, it will look normal. But if you make it spin a little slower, something funny happens: the top starts to flip over and over, like it’s doing a somersault in the air!

This weird flipping is called the Dzhanibekov Effect. It happens because the top isn’t perfectly balanced—it’s a bit like a pencil that’s not exactly the same on both ends. When it spins just right, it flips because of the way gravity and spinning work together in space.

So, the Dzhanibekov Effect is when a spinning object in space flips over and over because it’s not perfectly balanced!
